chunks: A group informed me, from Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn, who said: They informed us, Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Musa al-Daqqaq, and Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Sinani, and al-Husayn ibn Ibrahim ibn Ahmad ibn Hashim al-Mu'addib, from Abu al-Husayn Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Asadi al-Kufi (may Allah be pleased with him), that it was conveyed to him regarding the reply to his questions sent to Muhammad ibn Uthman al-Amari (may his spirit be sanctified):

As for what you asked about regarding the Prayer at the time of sunrise and sunset: If it is as the people say: 'The sun rises between the two horns of Satan, and sets between the two horns of Satan,' then nothing is better at rubbing the nose of Satan [disgracing him] than the Prayer. So pray it, and rub the nose of Satan.

key_terms.أَرْغَمَ أَنْفَ: Rubbed the nose of (idiom for disgracing)
key_terms.بَيْنَ قَرْنَيْ شَيْطَانٍ: Between the two horns of Satan

ai.seo_question: What is the wisdom behind praying at sunrise and sunset in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: This epistle from the Minor and Major Ghaiba highlights the Imam Mahdi’s (a.s.) pragmatic approach to fiqh, validating the popular cosmological metaphor of the sun rising between the 'horns of Satan' to justify the superiority of Salat during these times. By linking ritual prayer to the spiritual humiliation of Iblis, the text underscores the cosmic significance of daily worship in Shia tradition, where physical acts serve to diminish the influence of evil forces.

en.sayyid-athar-husain-s-h-rizvi: H 250 - A group of scholars informed me from Abu Ja’far Muhammad bin Ali bin Husain that he said: Narrated to us Ali bin Ahmad bin Musa Daqqaq and Muhammad bin Ahmad Sinani and Husain bin Ibrahim bin Ahmad bin Hashim Moddab from Abul Husain Muhammad bin Ja’far Asadi Kufi that it is mentioned that they sent some questions to Imam Mahdi (a.s); the following reply was received through Shaykh Abu Ja’far Muhammad bin Uthman Amari (q.s.):

As for a question you asked about the Prayer at the time of sunrise and sunset; its reply is as follows: It is said that the sun rises and sets between the two horns of Shaitan; so what is better than Prayer that it may rub the nose of Shaitan on the earth? Therefore pray at this time and rub the nose of Shaitan (disgrace him).
